description: Ambrosia is a Linux distro on Arch that looks and moves as one thing — one design authority, one token file, a generator theming every toolkit identically — shipped as Arch packages and an archiso installer image. The design system, preview and review site exist; the distro pipeline (packages, Ambrosia session on KWin, live image, installer) has a first cut; the shell has its menu bar.
features: Single OKLCH token file drives every toolkit theme identically
Generates GTK4, GTK3 light/dark, KDE colors, and QML shell theme
Generates fontconfig, FreeType env, web CSS, and resolved JSON
Gamut-maps colors to sRGB with contrast-derived accent variants
Solves response/damping springs into constants and easing curves
Validates contrast, concentric radii, and spacing grid via tests
Browser mock desktop preview styled only from generated tokens
Preview toggles dark mode and cycles accents via keys/URL
Preview blur-only control center, dock, tooltips and badges
Preview menus snap open instantly with right-click file menu
Review site renders spec with live specimens and verdict threads
Installs themes per-user on Linux preserving prior configs
Mac-first keyboard spec with Super-as-Command and switcher
Roadmap toward KWin/Quickshell shell, effects, and archiso image
Arch packages and an archiso live image that installs Ambrosia (UEFI), testable unattended in QEMU
Ambrosia session: Plasma's services with a Quickshell menu bar and wallpaper in place of plasmashell

preview.summary: Preview Desktop is a static HTML/JS mock macOS-like desktop for visually reviewing generated tokens. It renders draggable/focusable windows, menubar popups, sliders, control center, dock, and a live clock with no build step beyond `make build`. Every color, type, radius, shadow, and motion value comes from dist/web/tokens.css; preview.css holds only mock-desktop layout positions.

map.name: Mock desktop shell (wallpaper, menubar, dock, windows)
Control center (capsule modules, toggles, sliders, Edit Controls)
Dock (padding, glassy icons, tooltip, badges, separators)
Theme and accent switching (D / A keys, URL params)

flows.name: View updated tokens
steps: Run make build to regenerate dist/web/tokens.css
Open preview/index.html which links tokens.css + glass.css + preview.css
Toggle with D (dark mode) and A (accent cycle) to review

flows.name: Window interaction
steps: Click window to focus (preview.js manages z-order / active class)
Drag via titlebar to reposition (layout literals in preview.css)
Open menubar popups / sliders to check glass and controls

files: preview/index.html — mock desktop markup, SVG icon sprite, stylesheet links (requires dist/web/tokens.css)
preview/preview.js — theme/accent switching, popups, draggable windows, sliders, clock, squircle mask
preview/preview.css — mock-desktop layout; all design values via var(--amb-*) / var(--glass-*)
preview/glass.css — shared glass recipe (tint, blur, rim, edge, specular ring, grain)
rules: Never hardcode design values in preview/*.css — use vars from dist/web/tokens.css; only layout positions may be literals.
Run `make build` first — preview is broken/stale without generated dist/web/tokens.css.
Do not add build tooling or JS dependencies — static HTML/JS only.
Keep glass.css shared-safe — it is also used by the review site, so no preview-specific layout in it.
Round inner panels (e.g. sidebar) to their own outer corners — scaled-down blur is cut to the window shape only if the panel itself is rounded, otherwise corners render sharp/square.
Keep file selection highlight behind the icon — replacing the document page fill with selection color turns clicked icons black.
edges: Design Tokens via dist/web/tokens.css — sole source of colors, type, radii, shadows, springs; preview breaks without a build
Build and Install — `make build` generates dist/web/tokens.css that preview links

design-tokens.summary: Single-file source of truth for ambrosia's look and motion, exporting type scale, 4px spacing, radii, OKLCH colors, glass/materials, shadows, and springs. All dist themes are generated from it via tools/gen, so this file is edited instead of generated output. Newcomer must grasp: colors are OKLCH strings for perceptually even lightness and everything is light/dark Mode pairs.
files: design/tokens.ts — the single source of truth: font/type/tracking, space, radius, OKLCH color pairs, glass, shadow, springs
design/DESIGN.md — reasoning behind the numbers before retuning values
rules: Never hand-edit generated output in dist/; change design/tokens.ts and regenerate.
Keep colors as OKLCH strings (oklch(L C H) or with / A) so generator can convert and gamut-map to sRGB.
Provide both light and dark values via Mode/Pair for mode-dependent tokens.
See DESIGN.md for reasoning behind the numbers before retuning values.
Menus snap open instantly with no open animation (close fades 120ms); control-center panel is blur-only with no fill, border, or shadow, controls carry their own glass.
edges: Generator Core — resolves design/tokens.ts: OKLCH to sRGB, contrast, springs, dist orchestration
Theme Targets — format the resolved model into GTK, KDE, QML, fontconfig, web output
Preview Desktop — styled only from generated dist/web/tokens.css, never this file directly

review-site.summary: The Review Site is a design-review web app that renders every `## ` section of DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md as a reviewable item with live specimens, a verdict and a notes thread. Specimens are built with the same tokens and resolver the generator ships, so review matches output. State lives in `design/review.json` via a Bun server when present, otherwise in browser localStorage; `build.ts` emits a static fallback into `dist/site/`.

map.name: Review items sourced from design docs
Site styling in own design language

flows.name: Review a design item
steps: main.ts renders section with reasoning plus specimens
review.ts load() tries /api/review, falls back to localStorage
user sets verdict / posts note via setVerdict/addMessage
server.ts queues write into design/review.json or local mode saves locally
onChange listeners re-render verdict and thread

flows.name: Serve live review
steps: server.ts serves index.html with HMR on port 4747
STATIC preview/, dist/web/, assets/ served as plain files
POST verdict/message serialized through one write queue

flows.name: Build static review site
steps: no server: review.ts stays in localStorage mode

files: site/main.ts — page assembly, appearance switcher, verdict/thread UI wiring
site/specimens.ts — live token/resolver-driven examples per spec section
site/review.ts — verdict/thread state with server-then-localStorage fallback
site/server.ts — Bun server, hot reload, queued writes to design/review.json
site/content.ts — parses DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md headings into review items
site/site.css — review-site styling; values only from dist/web/tokens.css
site/build.ts — static build into dist/site/ plus preview asset copies
site/index.html — shell: sidebar, toolbar, content, wallpaper, sprite mounts
site/dom.ts — tiny h/s/icon element builder used by specimens
rules: Never hardcode review copy: items and intros come from DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md via content.ts.
No ad-hoc styling values: every value comes from dist/web/tokens.css, glass from preview/glass.css.
Verdicts are only approve/change/discuss (or null); server rejects anything else.
Review writes must go through the single queued writer; concurrent writes interleave otherwise.
Do not assume the server exists: static builds must keep verdicts/notes in localStorage.
Static build must copy preview, dist/web, assets/wallpapers or the preview iframe breaks.
edges: Design Tokens — specimens and accent list read design/tokens; review item source is DESIGN.md/DECISIONS.md
Generator Core — specimens render through tools/gen resolve, color, spring
Preview Desktop — embeds preview/index.html in iframe; reuses its icon sprite and preview/glass.css
Build and Install — static output lands in dist/site/; live site consumes dist/web/tokens.css
Theme Targets — specimens show what formatters will ship; review approves that output

build-install.summary: This layer installs the already-generated themes for the current Linux user into XDG config/data directories. It is a POSIX sh script that copies from dist/ with per-file backup of non-ambrosia files. The key idea: install never loses user data — foreign files become <name>.before-ambrosia, ambrosia-owned files are overwritten silently.

flows.name: Install themes
steps: Resolve dist/ relative to script location
Exit early (success) on non-Linux, pointing at dist/
Detect GTK mode via gsettings color-scheme (default light)
place() each dist artifact into XDG_CONFIG_HOME / XDG_DATA_HOME, backing up foreign files

files: tools/install.sh — installs dist/ themes per-user with .before-ambrosia backups and GTK light/dark pick
rules: Run from any cwd: dist path is derived from the script location, not cwd.
Non-Linux is not an error: exit 0 after pointing at dist/.
Only files lacking the 'Generated by ambrosia' marker are backed up; never delete a .before-ambrosia backup by overwriting blindly.
GTK3 gets only the active mode file copied as gtk.css; GTK cannot follow system scheme alone.
edges: Generator Core — install only copies dist/ output, never generates it
Theme Targets — dist gtk-3.0/gtk-*.css, gtk-4.0/gtk.css, kde colors are its install inputs
Linux desktop (XDG dirs, gsettings) — reads color-scheme, writes into XDG_CONFIG_HOME and XDG_DATA_HOME

theme-targets.summary: This layer turns the resolved theme model (Resolved/ResolvedMode from Generator Core) into per-toolkit output files. Each file in tools/gen/targets/ is a pure formatter: roles/colors plus shared helpers. Newcomers must grasp that nothing is resolved here — token truth and color math live upstream; targets only map and serialize.

map.name: Session kdeglobals (light scheme + type-scale fonts as QFont strings)

flows.name: Resolved model to toolkit file
steps: Target maps roles to toolkit vocabulary (libadwaita vars, KDE sets, QML tree, CSS vars)
Colors serialized via color helpers (toCss, toKde, toQtHex) and shared helpers (HEADER, pt, fontStack, kebab/slug)
Formatter returns file string for dist orchestration to write

files: tools/gen/targets/shared.ts — shared header, kebab/slug, fontStack, cssShadow, pt helpers
tools/gen/targets/gtk.ts — libadwaita CSS vars (gtk4) and named colors per mode (gtk3)
tools/gen/targets/kde.ts — opaque .colors sets, translucency flattened onto background
tools/gen/targets/qml.ts — Ambrosia QML singleton tree with Theme.dark / Theme.accentName switching
tools/gen/targets/web.ts — --amb-* CSS custom properties for preview/web surfaces
tools/gen/targets/fontconfig.ts — sans-serif/monospace aliases and rasterization defaults
rules: Do not edit generated output; every file carries HEADER pointing back to design/tokens.ts via tools/gen.
Do not resolve or derive colors here — use the passed Resolved model and color.ts / resolve.ts helpers.
KDE output must stay opaque r,g,b: flatten translucent values with flat() onto their background set.
GTK3 has no prefers-color-scheme: emit one file per mode; GTK4 emits light and dark in one file.
Keep QML identifiers safe: slug token keys and prefix leading digits.
QML property names can't be ECMAScript keywords; qml.ts suffixes them with _ (Theme.size.switch_), guarded by a test in tools/gen/rules.test.ts.
edges: Design Tokens — reads type, color, font, shadow token definitions as input vocabulary
Generator Core — consumes Resolved/ResolvedMode and color/spring serializers (toCss, toKde, toQtHex, toCssLinear, flat)
Build and Install — dist orchestration writes formatter output to dist/ for install

shell-and-session.summary: The desktop shell (Quickshell QML on the generated Ambrosia Theme module) and the session that hosts it. startambrosia runs Plasma's session with XDG_SESSION_DESKTOP=ambrosia; systemd units keyed on that variable swap plasmashell for Quickshell, and /etc/xdg/ambrosia (via XDG_CONFIG_DIRS) carries session-only KDE/KWin defaults. The shell must match preview/ visually.

map.name: Menu bar (logo, app name, menus, status icons, clock)
Line icons (same paths as the preview sprite)
Which windows/screens the shell puts up
Session start, env and defaults scope
KWin defaults (button order, hot corner, blur) and splash off
Session look-and-feel (colors, widget style, splash off)

flows.name: Login
steps: ambrosia-shell.service (ExecCondition) runs quickshell --path /usr/share/ambrosia/shell; plasma-plasmashell.service skipped by drop-in

flows.name: Look at it without logging in

rules: Build file URLs from Quickshell.shellDir with an explicit file:// — Quickshell's QML base URL is qrc:/qs-blackhole, so relative URLs and Qt.resolvedUrl don't reach files.
All values come from import Ambrosia (Theme.*); never hard-code colors or sizes that a token has.
KWin has no window-list protocol Quickshell reads (no wlr/ext foreign-toplevel), so ToplevelManager is empty; app name and dock dots need a KWin bridge.
KWin blur strength is global ([Effect-blur] in kwinrc), not per surface; BackgroundEffect.blurRegion only sets where.
edges: Theme Targets — imports the generated Ambrosia QML module (/usr/lib/qt6/qml/Ambrosia) and kdeglobals
Packaging and Image — ambrosia-shell installs shell/ to /usr/share/ambrosia/shell and session/ files system-wide
Preview Desktop — the visual reference the QML must match

packaging-and-image.summary: Everything that turns the repo into an installable distro. packaging/PKGBUILD builds ambrosia-theme, ambrosia-shell and ambrosia-desktop from the checkout; packaging/quickshell rebuilds Quickshell for the installed Qt. iso/ is an archiso profile (from Arch's releng) whose live system logs into Ambrosia and carries the packages as a local repo for its installer. Built on an Arch host (tenet), tested in a headless QEMU VM.

map.name: What each package installs and depends on
Package sources at build time and on the image ([ambrosia] first)
Live session: user, autologin, sudo, services
The installer: questions, then the install
Boot menu entries and kernel params

flows.name: Build
steps: tools/build-iso.sh copies iso/ to out/profile, repo-adds the packages into airootfs/opt/ambrosia/repo, fills @REPO@ in pacman.conf

flows.name: Install
steps: autostart Konsole runs ambrosia-install (kdialog questions, answers file with a password hash)
sudo ambrosia-install-system (sgdisk EFI+root, pacstrap from [ambrosia]+mirrors, user, systemd-boot, sddm state)

flows.name: Test
steps: tools/vm.sh install extracts the image's kernel and boots it with ambrosia.autoinstall (test answers, powers off)

rules: [ambrosia] must stay first in iso/pacman.conf: pacman takes a package from the first repo that has it, regardless of version, so our Quickshell rebuild only wins from there.
Quickshell links Qt internals: when Arch's quickshell was built for an older Qt than the system's, run make quickshell and ship ours.
Build and work dirs go under out/ on /home (tenet's / has ~25 GB); mkarchiso needs root, makepkg refuses it.
The installer is UEFI-only and needs the internet (pacstrap pulls everything but our packages from Arch mirrors).
edges: Shell and Session — ambrosia-shell ships shell/ and session/
Theme Targets / Generator Core — the PKGBUILD runs bun tools/gen/index.ts and installs dist/ system-wide
tenet (Arch build host) — reached with makima; tools/remote.sh rsyncs the checkout there
